description:
FUTURE / well-contained project. Replace/augment cl-ppcre (~3.7x behind Perl) with a PCRE2 backend bound via SBCL-native sb-alien (NOT CFFI — matches the existing crypt()→libcrypt bridge pattern). libpcre2-8/16/32.so.0 already present on the dev box; no -dev headers needed. Bind pcre2_compile_8 / pcre2_match_8 / pcre2_get_ovector_pointer_8 / pcre2_code_free_8. The FFI is easy; the real work is (1) UCS-4↔UTF-8 marshalling + byte-offset→char-index mapping for $&/pos/captures (cache encoded subject), (2) compiled-pattern GC lifetime + compile-constant-patterns-once (load-time-value). PREREQUISITE: first measure how much of the 3.7x is PCL plumbing (capture boxing, =~ *wantarray* wrap) vs the engine — only proceed if the engine dominates. Bonus over speed: PCRE2 is Perl-compatible, likely closes correctness gaps (/n, (?{…}), Unicode property classes; see not-supported.md). Full notes in docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md §8.
=== SPIKED AND MEASURED (s473q, Opus agent, 2026-09-07) ===
FULL REPORT WITH EVERY TABLE: docs/pcre2-spike-s473q.md.  No product code
changed; the spike lives in the agent worktree's scratch/s473q/.

THE VERDICT, ONE LINE.  On the configuration this task's binding list specifies
(no JIT) PCRE2 LOSES the risk case `subste` 1.188x against a control pair whose
spread is 0.6% -> the s473q stop rule's FIRST branch fires: cl-ppcre stays.
With pcre2_jit_compile_32 added PCRE2 WINS subste (0.972x), textproc (0.880x)
and json-rt (0.915x) and still LOSES regexg (1.134x), so the second branch's
precondition ("wins or ties (a) AND wins (b)/(c)") is not met either.  BOTH
readings agree: DO NOT BEGIN THE REPLACEMENT.

THE FFI IS EASY AND THE SEAM IS ONE FUNCTION - that half of this task is DONE.
  * libpcre2-32.so.0 through sb-alien (load-shared-object +
    define-alien-routine), the crypt()->libcrypt pattern.  No CFFI, no headers.
    pcre2_config_32(PCRE2_CONFIG_VERSION) = "10.46 2025-08-27"; JIT available.
  * THE 32-BIT WIDTH DELETES THIS TASK'S "HARD PART" (1): an SBCL
    (simple-array character (*)) is 32-bit code points, so with-pinned-objects
    + vector-sap is ZERO COPY and every ovector offset comes back as a
    CHARACTER INDEX.  Probed: \p{L}+ over "Î±Î²Î³ Î´ÎµÎ¶" gives ms=0 me=3.  No
    byte-offset->char-index map, no cached UTF-8 encoding.
  * Lifetime (2) is sb-ext:finalize per pcre2_code, one weak-pointer entry per
    pattern, cached in the op's %compiled slot exactly as today.
  * THE RUNTIME SWAP IS ONE FUNCTION.  %pcl-build-scanner returns a closure
    with cl-ppcre's (scanner function) protocol - (scanner string start end) ->
    (values ms me reg-starts reg-ends) - and END maps onto PCRE2's subject
    LENGTH, which IS ppcre's [START,END).  That one function carries m//, s///,
    do-scans, regex-replace(-all), %p-ppcre-scan and %pcl-scan-anchored-list.
    The perl pattern goes in VERBATIM: perl-regex-to-ppcre is not run.  Over
    the five bench programs: 8 distinct patterns compiled, 0 FALLBACKS, every
    output identical to perl's.

TWO MEASUREMENT BUGS THE SPIKE PAID FOR - DO NOT RE-DERIVE THEM.
  1. PCRE2_NO_UTF_CHECK IS A MATCH OPTION, NOT A COMPILE OPTION.  At compile
     time it only skips the PATTERN check; the SUBJECT is then re-validated on
     every pcre2_match, which is O(subject) per call and makes a /g loop
     QUADRATIC: /./g over 200k chars x5 read 41.9014 s checked vs 0.0570 s with
     the flag at match time (cl-ppcre 0.0270 s).  The price of passing it: SBCL
     strings can hold lone surrogates, whose behaviour under NO_UTF_CHECK is
     undefined.  A port owes a validity decision AT THE BOUNDARY.
  2. THE ZERO-COPY PROMISE HOLDS ONLY FOR (simple-array character (*)).  A
     simple-base-string subject must be WIDENED, and naively that copy is PER
     MATCH CALL: textproc went from cl-ppcre's 3.5 s to OVER SIX MINUTES.  The
     census: textproc hands over 42,840 base-string subjects (PCL's split scans
     one 200 kB base-string blob thousands of times).  Memoising the widened
     copy one-deep on identity fixed it (42,840 -> 6,006 widenings + 36,834
     hits) and is what every number here runs on.  This IS this task's budgeted
     "cached encoding", in a different currency - and an identity-keyed cache is
     UNSOUND for a base-string PCL mutates in place (a str-buffer).

(a)-(e) AT ROW LEVEL (scratch/s473q/ab-rt.pl: one transpile, two runtimes,
interleaved, startup subtracted, best-of-5; programs verbatim from
tools/bench-exec.pl).  Ratio = pcre2/cl-ppcre, BELOW 1.0 = PCRE2 faster.

  NO JIT                          ppcre     pcre2    ratio
    control(N=2000)              0.0129    0.0140    1.093
    subste  (a) tiny matches     0.2631    0.3127    1.188   <- THE RISK CASE
    regexg  (b) one long scan    0.7297    0.8989    1.232
    textproc(c)                  2.0962    2.0832    0.994
    json-rt (c)                  1.6245    1.4907    0.918
    pos100000 (e)                0.0963    0.1237    1.284
    pos200000 (e)                0.1190    0.1470    1.236
    control(N=2000) end          0.0155    0.0151    0.978
  (an independent earlier run: subste 1.185, regexg 1.267 - stable)

  WITH JIT (one binding beyond this task's list), control at a comparable
  absolute time so its spread is meaningful:
    control(N=40000)             0.3054    0.3074    1.006
    subste  (a)                  0.2680    0.2604    0.972
    regexg  (b)                  0.7975    0.9042    1.134
    textproc(c)                  2.1262    1.8716    0.880
    json-rt (c)                  1.6804    1.5372    0.915
    pos100000 (e)                0.1043    0.0961    0.922
    pos200000 (e)                0.1009    0.0961    0.953
    control(N=40000) end         0.3087    0.3098    1.003
  CONTROL SPREAD 0.3-0.6%, so every entry is real.

(d) PER-PATTERN COMPILE, 200 distinct literal patterns:
    cl-ppcre create-scanner  4.1 us   1.00x
    pcre2_compile            0.9 us   4.7x FASTER
    pcre2_compile + JIT      4.8 us   0.87x  (i.e. JIT brings the compile back
    to roughly cl-ppcre's price - which is what makes JIT affordable at load)

ENGINE ONLY (no PCL plumbing): PCRE2 WINS many-tiny-matches 1.15-1.24x (1.59x
JIT) and LOSES the long /./g scan 0.47x (0.54x JIT) - 27 ns vs 57 ns per /g
step, because each step is a fresh pcre2_match paying full match setup while
cl-ppcre's `.` scanner closure is trivial to re-enter.  regexg is the row that
scales the SUBJECT, i.e. exactly the shape PCRE2 is worst at.

PARITY - THE ARGUMENT THAT IS ACTUALLY STRONG.  perl's own t/re/re_tests, 1188
rows kept, PERL 5.40.3 ITSELF is the oracle (each verdict taken by running the
match in perl), replayed through PCL's cl-ppcre path and through PCRE2 verbatim
in one image, 5 s cap per row:
    both agree with perl                819  68.9%
    PCRE2 RIGHT, cl-ppcre WRONG         311  26.2%
    cl-ppcre right, PCRE2 wrong           7   0.6%
    both wrong                           51   4.3%
    cl-ppcre could not answer (ERR 197 + HANG 18)  215  18.1%
    PCRE2   could not answer (ERR 15, HANG 0)       15   1.3%
  cl-ppcre's misses by shape: plain 114, possessive/atomic 86, recursion 45,
  named/\g\k 22, control verbs 18, {n,m} 18, POSIX class 11, lookbehind 11,
  \N{} 10, \z\Z\A\G\b\B 8, backref 7, \p{} 6, \K 3, (?{}) 2, conditional 1.
  PCRE2's 15 refusals are short and enumerable: perl's charset modifiers
  (?u: (?l: (?d: (5, and /aa semantics give the only two WRONG ANSWERS),
  forward (?(1)a|b) with no group 1 (2), {37,17} n>m (1), \o{1_0000} (1),
  \p{nv=} / \p{L_}-family (2), one extractor artifact (m?...?).

  *** THE 18 HANGS ARE TASK #196 VERBATIM *** - .X(.+)+X, .X(.+)+XX,
  .XX(.+)+X, .X(.+)+[X] and friends, the re_tests catastrophic-backtracking
  block.  PCRE2 returns from all of them.  #71 IS #196's FIX, and neither task
  recorded that.

  RULE-12 NOTE A PORT MUST CARRY: pcre2_match returns a negative for
  PCRE2_ERROR_NOMATCH (-1) AND for MATCHLIMIT (-47) / DEPTHLIMIT (-53) /
  JIT_STACKLIMIT (-46).  The spike conflates them, which is why those rows read
  pcre2=n where perl says y.  A port MUST separate them and die/announce naming
  the code.

CONSTRUCTS not-supported.md NAMES #71 FOR (compile probe at 10.46):
  HAS: every control verb ((*FAIL) (*ACCEPT) (*SKIP) (*PRUNE) (*COMMIT)),
  (*script_run: / (*sr: / (*asr:, perl's /n (PCRE2_NO_AUTO_CAPTURE AND inline
  (?n)), \p{L} \p{Alphabetic} \p{Script=Greek} \p{L_}, possessive + atomic,
  (?R) and (?1), named captures with \k, \K, conditionals, variable-length
  lookbehind, POSIX classes, \N{U+0041}, and BOTH callout spellings (?C1) and
  (?C"str").
  LACKS: (?{ CODE }) and (??{ CODE }), \N{NAME}, \p{Word}, \p{IsGreek},
  \p{nv=}, (?u: (?l: (?d:, lenient {n,m}, \o{1_0000}.
  THE CALLOUT QUESTION, ANSWERED: PCRE2 refuses (?{ CODE }) outright but takes
  numeric/string callouts, and pcre2_set_callout on a match context is
  reachable by the same sb-alien technique (a callback).  So carrying (?{...})
  is POSSIBLE but not free: the pattern must be REWRITTEN to a numbered callout
  with the perl code held PCL-side.  A design item, not a binding.
  (?[ ... ]) COMPILES at 10.46 (10.45 added an extended-class syntax) but its
  semantics were NOT verified - do not count it either way.

PORTABILITY - AND THIS IS THE BLOCKER (measured with podman in each image):
  image          package        version              soname                  bare? after deps.sh?
  ubuntu:22.04   libpcre2-32-0  10.39-3ubuntu0.1     libpcre2-32.so.0.10.4   no    NO
  ubuntu:24.04   libpcre2-32-0  10.42-4ubuntu2.1     libpcre2-32.so.0.11.2   no    NO
  debian:12      libpcre2-32-0  10.42-1+deb12u1      libpcre2-32.so.0.11.2   no    NO
  debian:13      libpcre2-32-0  10.46-1~deb13u1      libpcre2-32.so.0.14.0   no    NO
  this dev box   libpcre2-32-0  10.46                libpcre2-32.so.0.14.0   yes   -
  1. libpcre2-8 IS in all four bare images (grep/git pull it in); libpcre2-32
     is NOT and the recipe's deps do not add it - deps.sh needs libpcre2-32-0.
     Cheap.
  2. THE VERSION SPREAD IS 10.39 -> 10.46 AND THE PARITY GAINS ARE ON 10.46.
     Variable-length lookbehind is 10.43+, the extended-class syntax 10.45+,
     several (?aX) modifiers 10.43+.  THREE OF THE FOUR SUPPORTED IMAGES SHIP A
     PCRE2 TOO OLD.  A floor (the PPI-1.291 pattern) would exclude
     ubuntu:22.04, ubuntu:24.04 and debian:12 from their own repositories; the
     alternatives are behaviour that VARIES BY OPERATING SYSTEM (strictly worse
     than cl-ppcre's uniform answer) or building/vendoring PCRE2 at install
     time, which the recipe does for nothing today.
  tools/install-pcl would have to load-shared-object + run one match AT INSTALL
  and refuse LOUDLY like the PPI floor - NEVER a silent fall-back to cl-ppcre,
  which is "both engines" by the back door.  dlopen name list, in order:
  libpcre2-32.so.0, libpcre2-32.so, libpcre2-32.0.dylib, libpcre2-32.dylib.
  macOS: Homebrew's pcre2 ships all three widths, BUT THERE IS NO macOS LEG IN
  CI AT ALL TODAY (grep -rn macos .github/workflows/*.yml finds nothing) - an
  engine change needs one first.  Musl/Alpine and the BSDs: REPORTED, not gated.

IF THIS IS EVER TAKEN, it is a PHASE for Fable to design, and its parts are:
ONE engine (never two at run time; a PCL_REGEX=ppcre switch may exist DURING
the migration as the A/B instrument and is DELETED at the end), JIT on (the
speed case depends on it entirely), the widened-subject cache with a soundness
rule, the error-code separation above, the callout rewrite for (?{...}), the
pos/\G protocol, the installer check, a version FLOOR, and the OS matrix +
a macOS leg.
